gaps.construct: global _O_TMPFILE_WORKS, read on every call and cleared after the first IsADirectoryError
gaps.description: The doc has no module-level variable and no way to declare in a header that an operation reads or writes shared state; 'module var' and listing it under uses are invented.

gaps.construct: eight parameters with defaults, one keyword-only (errors)
gaps.description: No defaults and no keyword arguments; every caller must pass all eight, and the positional order is easy to get wrong with several maybe Text parameters in a row.

gaps.construct: nested opener function passed to io.open that writes fd through nonlocal
gaps.description: No closures and no capture of a mutable outer variable; restructured so the descriptor is opened first and passed to open_stream, which changes the call graph of io.open.

gaps.construct: getattr(file, 'buffer', file), getattr(raw, 'raw', raw), raw.name = fd
gaps.description: No attribute lookup by name with a fallback and no setting a field on a dynamically reached inner object; left as a note, so the returned file's name is not set.

gaps.construct: io.open returns a file-like object whose concrete class depends on mode and buffering
gaps.description: No interface type; a closed choice FileObject is used, which callers must then choose on, unlike Python's duck-typed file.
No bitwise operators or flag-set type; 'flags with o_tmpfile without o_creat without o_excl' is invented.

gaps.construct: except OSError: pass (swallow and fall through to the fallback path)
gaps.description: The doc forbids an empty on failure line, but deliberately ignoring a failure and continuing is the intended behaviour; a dummy let is needed, which is exactly the filler the rule wants to prevent.

No catch-all for cleanup-and-rethrow; only the named OSError is handled, so interrupts and other exceptions would leak the descriptor. Hold-style cleanup does not fit because fd must survive on success.

gaps.construct: IsADirectoryError is a subclass of OSError, and except clauses are tried in order
gaps.description: The doc has flat named failures with no hierarchy; whether 'on failure OSError' also catches IsADirectoryError, and whether order matters, is not stated.

gaps.construct: returning an open file that the caller must close
gaps.description: Only hold (scoped release) and linear types are shown; there is no example of producing a linear resource to the caller from an operation that opens it, nor of a file deleted on close.

gaps.construct: fd = None then later assigned; mkstemp_inner returns a tuple (fd, name)
gaps.description: No tuple type or destructuring; 'produces a FileDescriptor and a Path' and 'fd of created' are invented.

gaps.construct: mode is a string tested with "b" not in mode
gaps.description: Replaced by a choice FileMode, which is safer but changes the parameter type and drops the many string modes.

gaps.construct: failures inside a handle block that are not named by any on failure line (OutOfMemory from open_stream)
gaps.description: The doc does not say whether an unnamed failure inside handle propagates to the operation's fails with list; assumed it does.

doc_rules_contradicted: An `on failure` line may not be empty: it must give back a value, fail, or call something. (satisfied only by a dummy let)
invented_syntax: module var o_tmpfile_works starts at true
uses files, memory, o_tmpfile_works (state listed as a capability)
flags with o_tmpfile without o_creat without o_excl
produces a FileDescriptor and a Path
fd of created (field access on a returned pair)
notes: This is the hardest of my set: it combines a process-wide cached feature flag, a callback that mutates an outer variable, reflection on the returned object, and catch-everything cleanup. The one-word-per-meaning rule fights the original's 'try the fast path, swallow the error, fall back' idiom, which needs an explicit 'ignore this failure' form. The capability style (files and memory passed in) works well and makes the header honest about what TemporaryFile touches.
